topics.summary: Security is the set of controls that preserves intended access and limits unintended consequences. blocks.text: Defense in depth uses several independent controls so one failure does not grant unlimited access. For HarborStatus, these include authenticated administration, limited service identity, read-only content, network policy, mandatory access control, updates, backups, and monitoring.

Independence matters. Two controls that rely on the same compromised account may fail together. A backup accessible for deletion with the production server’s credentials is not an independent recovery boundary. Draw the trust relationships and ask what remains protected after each component fails.
Linux example — 17.1
Inspect several independent security layers.

id
ss -lnt
stat -c '%a %U:%G %n' /etc/passwd

topics.title: 17.2 Least Privilege
topics.summary: Least privilege grants only the access needed for a defined task. A web worker reading static content should not own the operating system’s configuration or write the site’s release files. A monitoring account that reads a health endpoint does not need interactive root access.

blocks.text: Least privilege grants only the access needed for a defined task. A web worker reading static content should not own the operating system’s configuration or write the site’s release files. A monitoring account that reads a health endpoint does not need interactive root access.

Start with the required operation and resources, then grant narrowly. Do not infer that a failed operation needs “more privilege” before checking its path, identity, and configuration. An incorrect filename can produce a permission-like symptom that no sensible privilege policy should accommodate.

Review privilege granted to your account.

sudo -l

topics.title: 17.3 System Hardening
topics.summary: Hardening reduces unnecessary exposure and makes approved behavior explicit. Remove or disable unneeded services, restrict administration, protect configuration, apply supported updates, and validate the workload under the resulting policy.

blocks.text: Hardening reduces unnecessary exposure and makes approved behavior explicit. Remove or disable unneeded services, restrict administration, protect configuration, apply supported updates, and validate the workload under the resulting policy.

A hardening change needs a rollback and a functional test. Disabling a service because its name is unfamiliar can break time synchronization or identity. Use a baseline appropriate to the distribution release and server role, document exceptions, and test changes in a representative environment before fleet deployment.
Linux example — 17.3
Inventory exposed and enabled services.

systemctl list-unit-files --type=service --state=enabled --no-pager
ss -lnt
blocks.title: Original Linux example

blocks.text: What to check: Enabled services may not be running; sockets show actual listeners.

topics.title: 17.6 File Permissions
topics.summary: Permissions should reflect who must read, write, and traverse each path. Directory execute permission permits traversal; file execute permission permits execution. World-writable directories and overly broad recursive changes expand the set of people who can replace trusted content.

blocks.text: Permissions should reflect who must read, write, and traverse each path. Directory execute permission permits traversal; file execute permission permits execution. World-writable directories and overly broad recursive changes expand the set of people who can replace trusted content.

Configuration and executable files loaded by privileged services should not be writable by less-trusted users. A root-owned service unit pointing to a user-writable script still gives that user influence over privileged execution. Inspect the complete chain of files and parent directories, not only the unit file’s mode.

Trace a sensitive path's permissions.

topics.summary: Linux divides some traditional root powers into capabilities. A process may receive a particular privilege without receiving every root capability. This can reduce exposure when the capability is genuinely narrower than full root.

cards.question: What should you check after this section’s example?
cards.answer: A missing file capability can be normal; avoid granting broad capabilities to arbitrary binaries.

blocks.text: Linux divides some traditional root powers into capabilities. A process may receive a particular privilege without receiving every root capability. This can reduce exposure when the capability is genuinely narrower than full root.

Capabilities are still powerful and interact with namespaces, executable file attributes, and process state. Inspect with tools such as getcap where installed, and avoid granting broad capabilities merely to silence a failure. CAP_SYS_ADMIN encompasses many operations and should not be treated as a harmless convenience. Service-specific capability bounding can be part of a reviewed systemd policy. (R41)
Linux example — 17.7
Inspect process and executable capabilities when libcap tools are installed.

capsh --print
getcap /usr/bin/ping

topics.summary: A firewall evaluates traffic against policy. Decide which sources may reach which destinations, protocols, and ports, then implement that intent at the appropriate host and network boundaries. An allowed inbound port does not create a listening application.

blocks.text: A firewall evaluates traffic against policy. Decide which sources may reach which destinations, protocols, and ports, then implement that intent at the appropriate host and network boundaries. An allowed inbound port does not create a listening application.

State tracking commonly permits replies to established connections, but the exact policy depends on implementation. IPv4 and IPv6 both need consideration. Preserve management access and console recovery before changing host policy, and test from outside the host; local loopback traffic may follow different paths.

topics.title: 17.9 firewalld

blocks.text: firewalld manages host policy through concepts such as zones, services, ports, and runtime versus permanent configuration. Start with firewall-cmd --get-active-zones and inspect the zone attached to the actual interface or source.

A runtime change affects current policy; a permanent change affects what is restored later. They can differ. Do not assume that a permanent addition immediately opens a port, or that a temporary runtime rule survives reload. For an isolated lab, timed runtime changes can reduce forgotten exposure, but they do not replace a verified rollback. (R37)

sudo firewall-cmd --get-active-zones

topics.title: 17.15 Security Updates
topics.summary: Security maintenance requires supported repositories, advisories, testing, rollout, and verification that affected processes use the corrected code. Installing a library update does not necessarily replace an already-running process’s mapped copy. A kernel update normally requires booting into the new kernel unless an applicable supported live-patching arrangement addresses the issue.

topics.summary: Look for deviations connected to risk: unexpected administrative access, new listening services, unauthorized configuration changes, unusual outbound connections, and unexplained persistence. Compare against a known baseline and approved change records.

topics.title: 17.19 Incident Response Fundamentals
topics.summary: Incident response balances containment, evidence preservation, service impact, and communication. Identify the incident owner, record the initial facts, preserve relevant logs and volatile evidence as authorized, and choose containment that limits harm without destroying the investigation.

blocks.text: Incident response balances containment, evidence preservation, service impact, and communication. Identify the incident owner, record the initial facts, preserve relevant logs and volatile evidence as authorized, and choose containment that limits harm without destroying the investigation.

Do not immediately wipe or reboot every suspicious host. Those actions can remove useful evidence and may not remove stolen credentials or external access. Recovery often includes rebuilding from trusted sources, revoking affected credentials, closing the entry path, and verifying that monitoring works. Follow organizational and professional incident-response procedures for real events.

Begin a bounded incident evidence record.

who
ss -lnt
journalctl -b -n 50 --no-pager

labs.title: Reject a credential fixture with broad permissions
labs.code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
lab_dir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf -- "$lab_dir"' EXIT
cd -- "$lab_dir"
printf 'fixture secret\n' > credential
chmod 644 credential
test "$(stat -c %a credential)" != 600
chmod 600 credential
test "$(stat -c %a credential)" = 600
printf 'broad mode detected; private mode verified\n'
